_comment: Contract between mann1x/ollama and xollama. See FORK-SYNC.md (mann1x/xollama@dev).
patches[] ORDER IS APPLY ORDER. Merge each as its own --no-ff merge, in this order.
Two branches lack the up- prefix because they are heads of open cross-fork PRs:
renaming such a branch CLOSES the PR (measured 2026-09-21 on #18307). They get the
prefix if and when those PRs close.
status 'fork-only' means there is no upstream PR and none is planned: the patch
is ours to carry and upstream_pr is null. Every other entry is 'open-upstream'.

A patch whose changes cannot exist on the upstream tag gets a stacked up- branch: its row carries depends_on and a base that is the dependency set rather than the tag, the branch is built on the merge of exactly those dependencies AT THEIR MANIFEST SHAS, it is listed after all of them, and it is fork-only. up-response-scope-think-budget is the first.

integration.note: the last think-budget commit that changed code, which is the tree this patch set describes; the manifest commits after it touch only this file

release.note: cut before up-gemma4-unparsed-tool-call-content; it carries patches 1-12 only

verification.per_patch: go build ./... plus go vet and go test on every package the patch touches, run on the rebased branch at the sha below
verification.apply_order: the full sequence was replayed as sequential --no-ff merges from v0.34.2; see known_conflicts
verification.full_tree: v0.34.2 + patches 4, 5, 8, 14, 15, 16, 17 and the stacked 18, replayed as --no-ff merges: gofmt -l silent tree-wide, go build ./... clean, go vet ./... clean, go test ./... ok=56 fail=0 no-tests=22. Measured 2026-09-21 on solidPC (linux/amd64, root, tmpfs /tmp).

patches.title: llm: stop guessing that a repetitive payload is a runaway
server: do not hand over a tool call the model did not finish writing
gemma4: recover a finished tool call that is missing its closing brace
api: bound thinking with a token budget, per request or per model
mlx: link against libdl on linux
gemma4: do not answer with a channel name the parser was cut off from
qwen3coder: tolerate a dropped closing tag, and stop rewriting parameter values
llama: end a spent reasoning budget at a line, not mid-word
patches.note: 004 DRIFT CLOSED 2026-09-22 by up-response-scope-think-budget, which now carries the union. This branch keeps the upstream-facing surface -- the --reasoning-budget-scope flag and the THINK_BUDGET_SCOPE env var -- which ollama does not use because it sets scope per request over the wire; that is deliberate and stays. Correcting what this note said before: only ONE of the three commits was genuinely absent here. 677f91ce's C++ is SUPERSEDED (this branch has the later form; reset_tokens was renamed reset_seqs and the type generalised to vector<llama_tokens>, so an identifier test read it as missing). ca2e2cdb is OBSOLETE (it ports to b10242; LLAMA_CPP_VERSION pins b10969). b4c58eee was the real gap and is now carried.

patches.title: llm: send assistant thinking to the chat template
parsers: drop an unmatched thinking close tag instead of leaking it
server: reload when two tags share a blob but need different runner flags
gemma4: a tool call can open before the thinking channel is closed
qwen3.5: a tool call can open before the thinking channel is closed
gemma4: a tool call the parser cannot read must not vanish
parsers: let a parser name the tags its tool calls open with
launch: a session file stamped before the clock said start is not old
patches.note: Real defect, not a test artifact. codexAppRequestCursor.scan compares a filesystem mtime against a time.Now() taken moments earlier; tmpfs stamps mtime from the kernel's coarse clock, measured 4.55ms behind at CONFIG_HZ=250, so the rollout file is judged older than the session that just created it and skipped for the life of that session -- the count stays 0 however many prompts are sent. Two seconds of slack; the exact per-line filter is unchanged. Fixes TestCodexAppCountsOnlyOllamaRequestsInRegularProfile, which fails on any host whose temp dir is tmpfs. Not going upstream: ruled 2026-09-22, no PR to be filed. fork-only is the settled status, not a placeholder.

patches.title: fileutil: three permission tests assert the runner, not the code
patches.note: Test-only. TestWriteWithBackup_{PermissionDenied,FailsIfBackupFails,FileUnreadableButDirWritable} chmod a path then demand an error; root has CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and gets nil, so they fail for every build run as root, which is the container case. They already skip on Windows for the neighbouring reason; this folds both into one helper. Only those three -- the other twelve pass as root and still run. Measured after: root 12 pass 3 skip, unprivileged 15 pass 0 skip. Not going upstream: ruled 2026-09-22, no PR to be filed. fork-only is the settled status, not a placeholder.

patches.title: integration: gofmt vision_test_data_test.go
patches.note: One blank line. This is the only file `gofmt -l ./...` names on v0.34.2, so a silent-gofmt gate has to special-case it otherwise. Not going upstream: ruled 2026-09-22, no PR to be filed. fork-only is the settled status, not a placeholder.

patches.title: lfm2: keep a reasoning block out of the answer when thinking is off
patches.note: Carried from xollama@solidpc (mailbox #255). LFM2.5-8B-A1B reasons regardless of "think": false -- its official chat template has no off switch -- so setInitialState routed the whole <think> block verbatim into content. This discards it when thinking is off and the parser supports thinking, the way gemma4.go and laguna.go already do. Independent of every other patch: it touches only lfm2.go, in three hunks that miss up-think-budget's ThinkingTags addition, plus an additive test; base is v0.34.2 and there are no known_conflicts. Six new tests, three fail on the unpatched parser. Whether it goes upstream is the repository owner's call; fork-only until then, not a placeholder.

patches.title: llama: load a gemma-4 assistant drafter whose shape is left unchecked
patches.note: Carried from xollama@solidpc (mailbox #284; authored there as a836824b). A llama.cpp patch, so it retires on a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump: check_tensor_dims read gemma4-assistant's empty expected shape {} as 'must be a scalar', and its error path threw vector::_M_range_check from llama_format_tensor_shape(ne), so an E2B/E4B assistant drafter never loaded. The .patch blob (4f103fa6) is byte-identical to xollama's. The applier sorts by file name, so 005 applies after 001, models/003 and 004 regardless of merge order; replayed on a clean b10969 fetch (391fac16) with 001+003+004+005 and llama-server built. Independent of every other patch; its one collision is the README entry, see known_conflicts. Merge position here only follows the fork-only-before-stacked convention.

base.note: NOT the upstream tag, and cannot be: this patch calls parsers.ToolCallStartTagForParser (added by up-toolcall-tags) and extends the reasoning-budget request plumbing of up-think-budget and up-reasoning-budget-line-boundary. The branch is built on the merge of exactly those three at the shas above, so it merges cleanly only after all three and is listed last for that reason.

patches.title: llm+llama: spend the thinking budget across a response, not per block
patches.note: Go half AND llama.cpp half. The feature lived on think-budget and on no up-* branch; this is the extraction. The Go half is a no-op for think-budget (all 77 added lines verified already present). The 004 patch is regenerated against the b10969 pin and applies to a pristine b10969 with no fuzz; it is the UNION of #18212's copy and think-budget's, which closes the drift flagged on #18212's row. VERIFIED BY BUILD: cmake -DGGML_CUDA=OFF, target test-reasoning-budget, 14/14 pass; reverting the two behaviours fails test-reasoning-budget.cpp:367. Go gates cannot see a .patch, so a build is the only check that can. INTEGRATED 2026-09-25: think-budget never took this branch's 004 until cherry-pick -x dea66221; until then the integration branch and the v0.34.2-1-thinkbudget runtime carried the pre-drift 945-line copy. think-budget's 004 is now byte-identical to this branch's (blob c5e6c902).

known_conflicts.resolution: both patches add a new top-level test function at the same point; keep both blocks. Reversing the order conflicts identically -- this is not an ordering mistake.
same shape: two additive test blocks at the same point. Keep both. Reversing conflicts identically.

same shape again, three files at once: up-think-budget adds ThinkingTagger and the ThinkingTags methods, up-toolcall-tags adds ToolCallTagger and the ToolCallTags methods, both at the same point. Keep both, ThinkingTagger first. NOTE the boundary cuts inside a function: the closing brace on the line after >>>>>>> belongs to BOTH halves, so close the first block with its own brace rather than concatenating the two sides -- a plain keep-both here produces code that does not parse.

both add a Files entry after 002's. Keep both, 004's entry first, so the list reads in apply order. Replayed from v0.34.2 as --no-ff merges: the result is blob d612923f, byte-identical to xollama's README at a836824b.
